description: baseline

n=512 B=640 is the dominant geomean weight (4 of 12 shapes: dense 3310us, mixed 5237, rankdef 2830, clustered 2127) and is panel-factorization-bound (~53%). ncu-profile the n512 mixed driver first, then attack the panel: cut the serial reflector-chain latency (wider outer blocks, fewer barriers/syncs per panel) and pool all 640 matrices into one device-wide cuBLAS batched tensor-core trailing GEMM. Hold trailing-GEMM precision fixed; this is a latency+batching win, not a precision win.

OB=128 wider outer block on n512 dense good path. VALIDATION FAILED: diff_correctness + invariance guards flag factor residual ~31 (scaled ~1250 >> gate 0.5) on n512 dense/mixed/rankdef/clustered. Root cause: PAF panel+apply fusion only fires when inner_rest<=INNER_WMMA_NTMAX=64; at OB=128/IB=16 inner sub-panels have inner_rest up to 112>64, falling to standalone panel + cuBLAS inner apply which mishandles the 128-wide outer-V fold geometry. Reverting to baseline.

IB=32 wider inner block on n512 dense good path (OB=64 kept). Validation PASS (all 3 guards). REGRESSION: shape3 dense 3306->3926us (+19%), geomean 1761->1784. Halving PAF launches did not pay off: dense falls off the IB=16-specific fill_R_zero_tail to generic tiled fill, longer per-launch serial chain not hidden at waves<1, 32-wide WMMA apply no more efficient. Honest regression committed.

Brief-0 (n512 block-geometry) exhausted. Both levers FAILED: OB=128 breaks correctness (PAF fusion ceiling inner_rest<=64; falls to standalone apply that mishandles 128-wide outer-V geometry, factor residual ~31 >> gate). IB=32 validates clean but REGRESSES dense +19% (geomean 1784 vs 1761). KEY FINDING from clean dense profile: qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel (panel-factor + inner WMMA apply, fused) is 50.3% of n512 dense; trailing GEMMs (nvjet_hsh) already small+batched. PAF is latency-bound: 640 CTAs, 0.86 waves/SM, occupancy 49% capped by Block-Limit-Registers=5 (48 regs/thread), compute 47% / mem 48% (neither saturated). The panel is the bottleneck exactly as the brief said, but block-geometry knobs cannot fix it -- the serial BLAS-2 reflector chain per CTA is the real cost. Recommend: convert the panel to BLAS-3 (CholeskyQR-style Gram+chol) for the well-conditioned good subset, OR reduce PAF registers to lift occupancy past 1 wave.

n=512 B=640 good subset is panel-factorization-bound (~53%, BLAS-2 serial-reflector chain); block-geometry tuning is exhausted (OB=128 hits the hard inner_rest<=INNER_WMMA_NTMAX=64 fusion ceiling, IB=32 regressed +19%). Replace the FP16 two-level panel on the WELL-CONDITIONED good subset with CholeskyQR2 (TF32 SYRK Gram, chol, A*R^-1, repeat once for orthogonality) + orhr_col reconstruction, converting the panel into device-saturating BLAS-3. CRITICAL: do NOT attempt all-CholeskyQR; KEEP the existing classify_convert_n512 good/bad split and route ONLY well-conditioned members to CholeskyQR2, leaving the ill-cond bad subset on the existing geqrf/exact fallback (escalate marginal good members to shifted-CholeskyQR3, do not abandon the split). Reuse the already-working _cholqr_path (L6322) + _choleskyqr_1pass (L6286) orhr_col/PD-gate/bad-row-geqrf machinery — this is a PORT to n=512, not from scratch. Parent stacks on W1's n=32 graph win (1742us). Profile GEMM utilization with ncu.

CholeskyQR2+orhr_col with Python whole-batch PD/colnorm/finite gate + geqrf fallback. Validation PASS. MASSIVE REGRESSION: geomean 1742->7055. n512 dense 3306->74253us(22x), mixed->359124, rankdef->916147, clustered->81528. Gate falls back to torch.geqrf for most matrices incl cond=2 dense (FP32 Cholesky of G=A^TA with cond~1e6-1e8 is non-PD/marginal); per-rep A[bad_idx] gather+cuSOLVER geqrf at B=640 is catastrophic. Need to diagnose fallback rate and route via C++ classify good subset instead of whole-batch gate. Honest regression committed.

Shifted-CholeskyQR3 (column-equilibrate + pass-1 Fukaya shift -> always-PD pass1; plain passes 2/3 -> orthogonality; pass-2 non-PD gate bails ill-cond batches to C++ driver; geqrf for residual bad: dense 6/640, clustered 11/640). TF32 Gram, nb=64 TRSM. Validation PASS (all guards). REGRESSION geomean 1742->3942: n512 dense 3306->54370us (16x). NEGATIVE FINDING: CholeskyQR not competitive at n512 B640. Profile: SIMT 32x32 sgemm 41% (tri_solve_right_inv diagonal solve does NOT tensor-core at n512 block sizes), geqrf+cuSOLVER ~45%, 3x potrf+Grams+orhr_col rest. 6 Grams+3 triangular solves+3 Cholesky+orhr_col LU recon = far more total work than the existing BF16-tensor-core PAF path (3.3ms); TRSM/Cholesky/recon not GEMM-bound so BLAS-3 advantage never appears.

Brief-1 (CholeskyQR2 on n512 good subset) EXHAUSTED with a clear NEGATIVE FINDING. Ported the existing orhr_col/_cholqr_path machinery to n512, made it CORRECT (column-equilibrate + Fukaya pass-1 shift -> always-PD Cholesky; plain passes 2/3 -> FP32 orthogonality, dense orth 7e-6; pass-2-nonPD gate bails ill-cond batches to the C++ driver; geqrf for the few residual bad: dense only 6/640). Validation PASSES all guards. But it REGRESSES hard: n512 dense 3306->54370us (16x), geomean 1742->3942. ROOT CAUSE (microbenchmarked at n512 B640): only the Gram is fast/BLAS-3 (TF32 As^T@As = 0.29ms); the batched Cholesky (potrfBatched 3.98ms) and the triangular solve Q=A R^-1 (~5ms via custom blocked, torch solve_triangular, OR explicit-inverse+GEMM -- all ~5ms, the solve is inherently column-sequential and does NOT tensor-core at n512 sizes) dominate. CholeskyQR2 = 2x(0.29+3.98+5) ~18ms, QR3 ~28ms, plus orhr_col recon -- vs the existing BF16-tensor-core PAF blocked-Householder at 3.3ms. Even ONE CholeskyQR pass (~9ms) loses to PAF. The brief's BLAS-3 hypothesis holds only for the Gram; Cholesky+TRSM are the wall. RECOMMENDATION: abandon CholeskyQR for n512. The PAF panel (50% of dense, latency-bound at 0.86 waves/SM, occupancy 49% capped by Block-Limit-Registers=5 @ 48 regs/thread) is better attacked by (a) cutting PAF register pressure to lift CTAs/SM past 1 full wave, or (b) the n512-specific fill_R kernel + classify overhead (classify_convert 5%, fill 2.7%). geqrf is catastrophic at B=640 (951ms whole-batch) -- any future path must avoid per-rep geqrf on large subsets.

n512 dense panel is at the serial-reflector-latency wall (occupancy/precision/CholeskyQR all dead). Redirect to the MIXED n512 shape (5237us = ~1900us MORE than dense 3310us): qr_n512_mixed_driver runs the exact-FP32 bad-subset blocked_qr_2level (OB64/IB32 cmf panel) FULLY SERIAL after the good FP16 subset. Profile the bad-subset COUNT and the bad-path time first to confirm the ~1900us. Then attack it: (1) the small bad subset underfills the GPU, so OVERLAP the good FP16 and bad exact-FP32 factorizations via a CUDA GRAPH -- build the good-chain and bad-chain as independent node sequences with NO dependency edges between them and launch on the NULL queue (literal 0); NEVER use CUDA streams (the harness bans the 'stream' substring). WATCH the shared mutable g_* panel-config globals (set_n512_good_flags vs set_n512_bad_flags incl g_panel_cmf/g_qr2_no_clone) -- concurrent nodes can't both read correct flag state, so bake per-path config into kernel args or fully configure each before the other's nodes run. (2) Fallback if the good path already saturates all 148 SMs (overlap can't help): shrink the bad-path per-matrix cost directly, or tighten an over-conservative classifier that flags too many matrices as bad. Stacks on the n=32 graph global best.

WIN: route soft b_mid matrices to FP16 good subset. The n512 classify_decide gate sent b_mid (mid_ratio<1e-9: clustered/rank-deficient) to the slow exact-FP32 bad subset; but b_mid is not an FP16-killer (FP32-V reflectors orth-exact), measured 0/62 mixed b_mid matrices fail factor/orth on the FP16 path. Changed bad=hard (drop ||b_mid). Mixed n512 5237->4988us (-4.8%), geomean 1742->1736 (parent), 1764->1736 vs baseline. Profile confirmed STEP1: good region 2860us THEN serial bad region 2510us; b_mid was bloating the bad subset (175->113 hard). dense/rankdef/clustered unchanged. Validation PASS all 3 guards.

Brief-2 EXHAUSTED with a committed WIN (e50f82f, geomean 1742->1736, MIXED n512 5237->4988us -4.8%, validated all 3 guards). STEP1 confirmed mixed = two serial phases (good FP16 ~2860us THEN exact-FP32 bad ~2510us). WIN: the classify_decide gate over-routed b_mid matrices (clustered/rank-deficient-via-tiny-mid-column) to the slow exact-FP32 bad subset; b_mid is NOT an FP16-killer (FP32-V orth-exact), measured 0/62 mixed b_mid matrices fail factor/orth on FP16 -> changed bad=hard, bad subset 145->95. PRIMARY LEVER (CUDA-graph overlap) INFEASIBLE: both good+bad chains are ~45-50% cuBLAS batched GEMMs (good nvjet_hsh BF16; bad Kernel2+cutlass simt FP32) which CANNOT be added as cudaGraphAddKernelNode nodes (only single custom kernels can); cuBLAS graph-capture needs cudaStreamBeginCapture (banned 'stream' substring); null queue serializes. The n=32 graph trick (pure custom kernels) does not generalize to GEMM-heavy chains. Bad-path precision-shrink REJECTED: TF32 trailing documented to fail band/rowscale remotely, and the bad subset is now exactly those hard FP16-killers. Bad-path cmf panel config is tuned (g_panel_defer doesn't apply to the FP32 path). NOT pursuing the speculative all-custom-kernel bad+good trailing rewrite (large, high-regression-risk, likely slower than cuBLAS -- negative EV). RECOMMENDATION: the n512 floor is now good_region(~2943us, the dense panel wall) + bad_region(~1819us); both serial, overlap blocked by the cuBLAS/stream constraint. Further n512 gains need either a graph-able all-custom trailing (risky) or attacking the shared good-region panel wall (brief-0/1 showed that's hard).

Redirect off the n512 latency wall to the UNOWNED n=2048 B=8 (7362us, 2nd biggest shape). It is SM-STARVED: only ~8 matrix-CTAs against 148 SMs, so the panel/trailing chain is latency-exposed with the device underfilled -- an OCCUPANCY/throughput regime (unlike n512's grid-saturated latency wall) where there is real room. The path already uses the cm_coop pivot panel + yfold and is ~88% GPU-busy, so the easy knobs are partly spent; the UNEXPLORED lever is to POOL the 8 matrices' independent trailing GEMMs (S=V^TC, W, build_Minv, Y=MW, C-=VY) across the whole device the way set_n512_good_flags does for n512 (cuBLAS batched/strided GEMMs spanning all 8 matrices at once instead of per-matrix launches), and/or a multi-CTA m-split on the wide outer trailing apply to fill idle SMs. Keep FP16-V (orth-exact); factor gate unchanged. Profile n2048 launch-idle + GEMM occupancy with ncu first. Stacks on your banked mixed-n512 win (1736).

n2048 IB=16 throughput-shift test. STEP1 ncu confirmed: panel (cm_coop) is 65% of n2048 and SM-starved (8 CTAs/148 SMs, 0.05 waves, 3.3% SM throughput = LATENCY-bound serial column chain); trailing GEMMs already cublasGemmStridedBatched over B=8 (brief premise corrected). IB=16 hypothesis (shrink within-panel BLAS-2 m*IB^2, shift to GPU-filling trailing) REGRESSED: n2048 7346->8062us, geomean 1736->1751. IB=16 doubles panel-launch count -> more SM-starved serial-chain exposure. Confirms the panel is a serial-LATENCY wall (same as n512), not a within-panel throughput problem -- multi-CTA m-split (throughput lever) cannot fix a latency-bound chain and would add per-column inter-CTA sync latency. Reverting to IB=32.

Revert IB to 32 (parent perf restored: n2048 7345us, geomean 1737). Brief-3 conclusion: trailing GEMMs already strided-batched over B=8; the cm_coop PANEL (65%, SM-starved 8 CTAs/0.05 waves, 3.3% SM throughput) is LATENCY-bound on the serial per-column reflector chain; IB=16 throughput-shift regressed to 8062us; multi-CTA m-split would add per-column inter-CTA sync latency to a latency-bound chain (ruled out by IB=16+ncu evidence). Same serial-reflector wall as n512. Recommend recursive/CAQR panel (tree-combine) as next direction. Validation PASS all guards.

Brief-3 (n2048 occupancy) EXHAUSTED at parent perf (geomean 1737, n2048 7345us; no regression carried). FINDINGS: (1) brief premise CORRECTED -- the n2048 trailing GEMMs (S/W/Y/C-=VY) are ALREADY cublasGemmStridedBatched over all B=8 (single batched launches), not per-matrix; the brief's primary 'pool the trailing GEMMs' lever was already done. (2) ncu STEP1: the cm_coop PANEL is 65% of n2048, SM-starved (8 CTAs/148 SMs, Waves 0.05, 3.3% SM throughput) = LATENCY-bound on the serial per-column reflector chain (same wall as n512's 50% PAF). trailing=20% (already batched, wide apply fills), build_Minv=13%. (3) TESTED the throughput-shift lever: IB=16 REGRESSED n2048 to 8062us (more/smaller SM-starved panels = more serial-chain launch exposure) -- committed honest (c2653d4), reverted. (4) RULED OUT multi-CTA m-split: it addresses throughput, but the panel is LATENCY-bound (the IB=16 regression + 3.3% throughput prove it), and per-column inter-CTA sync (grid.sync, ~4096 syncs, no cooperative-launch infra present) would ADD latency to a latency-bound chain -- net negative. CAQR/RECURSIVE-PANEL ASSESSMENT (manager's higher-ceiling idea): the existing two-level WY already de-serializes the T-formation (build_Minv batched, replaces larft j-recurrence) but the cm_coop PANEL's serial IB-column loop is the wall. A recursive Elmroth-Gustavson panel converts that to BLAS-3 tree-combines, BUT at IB=32/B=8 the tree GEMMs are tiny (underfill); it only fills the GPU with a WIDE panel (IB>=128) = a re-blocking into 3 levels, and even then B=8 may underfill the tree GEMMs. orhr_col (H,tau)-reconstruction machinery exists to recover the compact factor. Tractability: MODERATE-TO-HARD (tight existing two-level code; needs re-blocking + a new recursive panel kernel; B=8 underfill risk persists). It is the one genuinely-untried structural lever for the serial-reflector wall across n512+n2048+n1024 -- recommend it as the next brief if the ceiling justifies the rewrite risk.

THE big structural bet: break the serial per-column reflector dependency that is the wall on EVERY medium/large shape (n512 PAF 50%, n1024 59%, n2048 65%) and the likely source of #1's 25% edge. Replace the n512 GOOD-path serial column-by-column panel (PAF/cm) with a RECURSIVE Elmroth-Gustavson Householder panel: split the OB-wide panel's columns in half, recurse left -> (V_L,T_L,R_L), apply the block reflector (I-V_L T_L V_L^T)^T to the right half as ONE batched tensor-core GEMM across all 640 matrices, recurse right, combine T=[[T_L,-T_L V_L^T V_R T_R],[0,T_R]]. This converts the panel's serial BLAS-2 chain into BLAS-3 tree-combines that, batched across B=640, FILL the device (n512 is the BEST-fill regime -- W0's own analysis: tree GEMMs underfill at B=8/n2048 but not B=640). KEY: a recursive HOUSEHOLDER panel emits (V,T) DIRECTLY -> tau=diag(T) -> slots into the existing compact-WY build_Minv/trailing-apply framework; NO orhr_col, NO CholeskyQR (both proven dead). Keep the good/bad split + your mixed-classifier win; recursion base case = a few cols (tiny serial). Keep FP16/FP32-V (orth-exact), factor gate unchanged. If it wins on n512 it generalizes to n1024/n2048. ncu the new panel's tree-GEMM fill. Highest-ceiling, moderate-to-hard; you are the natural owner (deepest panel-wall knowledge). Stacks on global best 1736.

OB=128 wide panel w/ batched cuBLAS inner applies (the recursive panel's prerequisite). FIXED brief-0 OB>64 fill bug (off-diagonal fast path covered only 64 of OB cols). RESULT: REGRESSES dense 3306->4598us (+39%), geomean 1736->1782. At OB=128 PAF can't fuse (inner_rest>64) so inner applies become separate batched cuBLAS GEMMs (launch overhead + HBM round-trips) vs fused on-chip PAF (V resident in smem). FALSIFIES wide-panel-with-batched-applies for n512 -> the recursive Elmroth-Gustavson panel (same batched cuBLAS tree-combines) cannot win for n512 either. Validation PASS all guards. Reverting OB to 64.

Revert OB to 64 (restore global best 1734, dense 3305 mixed 4991, all guards pass). Brief-4 recursive-panel bet FALSIFIED for n512: the batched tree-combine mechanism (tested via OB=128 batched cuBLAS inner applies) regressed dense +39%. For 640 small matrices the factorization is already optimally batched (640 CTAs) with the fused on-chip PAF (V in smem, no HBM round-trip); off-chip batched cuBLAS applies add launch+HBM overhead that dominates. All recursion variants covered: batched-tree=OB128-falsified, on-chip-tree=same-PAF-latency-wall, multi-CTA=brief3-ruled-out. Kept the latent OB>64 fill-bug fix. Recursive panel is the wrong tool for small batched matrices.

Brief-4 (recursive Elmroth-Gustavson panel for n512) EXHAUSTED -- the big structural bet is FALSIFIED for n512, at global best 1734 (no regression carried; +a latent fill-bug fix). The recursion's core mechanism (batched tensor-core tree-combine GEMMs replacing the serial panel) was tested via OB=128 with batched cuBLAS inner applies: REGRESSED dense +39% (3306->4598us). Decisive because the recursion's tree-applies ARE batched cuBLAS GEMMs (per the brief), and OB=128 exercises exactly that mechanism. ROOT CAUSE: for 640 SMALL matrices the factorization is ALREADY optimally batched (640 CTAs) by the fused on-chip PAF megakernel, which keeps V resident in smem (NO HBM round-trip); moving the inner applies off-chip to batched cuBLAS GEMMs adds per-apply launch overhead + trailing-block HBM read/write that DOMINATES at these sizes (the existing code already caps inner_wmma_wmax=32 to keep inner applies fused, routing only the OB-wide outer apply to cuBLAS -- this run independently re-derived why). ALL recursion variants covered: (1) host-orchestrated batched tree-applies = the OB=128 mechanism (falsified, +39%); (2) in-kernel on-chip tree-applies = a more complex PAF, same 1-CTA/matrix latency wall (0.86 waves), serial reflector chain identical; (3) multi-CTA-per-matrix tree = per-column inter-CTA sync, ruled out brief-3 (IB=16 regression + 3.3% SM throughput). FIXED a latent correctness bug en route: fill_above_panel_R_tiled_kernel's off-diagonal fast path covered only 64 of OB columns (FP32-garbage R at OB>64); gated to OB==64 + column-looping path for OB>64 -- kept (harmless latent-bug fix). CONCLUSION: the serial per-column reflector chain for 640 small batched matrices is irreducible and ALREADY optimally handled by the fused PAF; the recursive panel is the wrong tool here (it shines for FEW LARGE matrices, not many small ones). The n512 good path (and the whole medium/large-shape panel) is at the speed of light for this algorithm class. Recommend: stop attacking the panel; the remaining gap to #1 (if any) is elsewhere (e.g. the mixed bad-subset, or a fundamentally different factorization the leader may use). My banked mixed-classifier win (1736) stands as the run's n512 contribution.

Panel is speed-of-light (4 angles falsified) -- attack the n512 MIXED bad-subset's biggest addressable chunk. FALSE-BAD found: clustered matrices fire b_mid (mid_ratio<1e-9 at col 320, scaled to ~eps) and take the ~2166us exact-FP32 path, BUT the code PROVES homogeneous clustered factors correctly+fast on the capped-FP16 rank-reveal path (ncap=320, hard_bad==0, L1181). Same matrices, ~10x cost gap. In qr_n512_mixed_driver, split the bad set into hard_bad (b_row/b_cos/b_off -> exact FP32, UNCHANGED) and b_mid-ONLY (clustered -> a SECOND indexed capped-FP16 rank-reveal good pass via blocked_qr_2level_bf16_indexed with the tailmask ncap, exactly as the homogeneous path does). b_mid_count=bad_count-hard_bad is ALREADY available at the existing D2H (counts[3]=hard_bad); you need to emit a separate b_mid index list (currently b_mid+hard share bad_idx). Target: move ~53/640 matrices off the serial FP32 tail wave, shrinking the bad subset ~50% on the mixed shape (4988us). Watch the bad_count*16>B*15 near-all-bad fallback (already branches on hard_bad==0). VALIDATE mixed + homogeneous-clustered + rankdef (must not misclassify any genuine FP16-killer to the fast path -- all guards pass). Stacks on global best 1734.

Brief-5 (cap b_mid clustered false-bad in the mixed bad-subset) EXHAUSTED by MEASUREMENT: the win is ALREADY BANKED in my brief-2 commit, and the residual is net-negative. (1) The brief's premise -- b_mid clustered stuck in the slow exact-FP32 bad subset -- was true of the ORIGINAL code, but my brief-2 change (bad=hard, dropping ||b_mid) already moved ALL b_mid-only matrices OUT of the bad subset INTO the good FP16 subset. Confirmed on parent 4ef1a53: mixed split is good=545 (483 dense + 62 b_mid clustered), bad=95 (genuine hard FP16-killers ONLY; cmf grid=95). The ~50% bad-subset shrink the brief targets (145->95) and the mixed improvement (5237->4988) ALREADY HAPPENED in brief 2. (2) The only residual is capping the 62 b_mid clustered (rank-reveal ncap~256) WITHIN the good pass (they currently factor full-512). DIRECT IN-CONTEXT MEASUREMENT: good pass with the 62 clustered (527 matrices full-512)=2.970ms vs dense-only (465)=2.828ms => the 62 clustered cost only 0.138ms MARGINAL in the fused good pass (they share the batched trailing GEMMs + their tail cols are ~eps so FP16 work is trivial). Capping saves AT MOST ~half of 0.138ms ~= 0.07ms (~0.1% geomean), and a SEPARATE rank-reveal-capped indexed pass (62 matrices, underfilled at 62 CTAs) would LOSE the fusion benefit + add launch overhead -> NET-NEGATIVE. (3) The remaining 95 bad matrices are genuine FP16-killers (b_row/b_cos/b_off); the brief + code forbid the fast path (TF32/FP16 over the factor gate remotely). NO safe false-bad left. DID NOT implement a measured-net-negative 3-way classify split (poor EV + regression risk; reported to manager for the call). HEAD stays at global best 1734. Brief-5's intended win was captured one brief early (brief 2).

n512 incremental levers are mined out (panel speed-of-light, classifier false-bads banked, bad-path exact-FP32 floored, no concurrency). Take the BOLD bet at the 25%-to-#1 gap: the checker requires ONLY (a) Q=householder_product(H,tau) orthogonal and (b) triu(H)~Q^T A -- it does NOT require H's strict-lower V to be the TRUE Householder reflectors of A. The submission already exploits this once (the n4096 tau-override: exact tau-from-V makes Q orthonormal regardless of V precision). GENERALIZE that freedom to the n512 BAD subset (~95 hard FP16-killers, ~2166us serial exact-FP32, ~43% of mixed): instead of an exact-FP32 Householder factorization, find a CHEAPER route to SOME valid (V,tau,R) for those matrices. Candidate: factor in FP16/TF32 to get an approximate Q,R, then APPLY the tau-override trick (recompute tau exactly from the produced V so householder_product is orthonormal by construction) so ONLY the loose factor residual (rtol=20*512*eps) binds -- the bad matrices failed the gate in pure FP16 on the FACTOR residual, but if the tau-override + a cheap correction (e.g. one refinement of R against Q^T A) holds that residual, the exact-FP32 path is avoided. MUST genuinely factor each input (the diff_correctness/invariance/offgrid guards forbid memorized/content-dispatch hacks); verify all guards + the remote-safe margin. If FP16+tau-override can't hold the factor gate for rowscale/band/nearcollinear, report it as tested. Early-exit allowed if it proves dead in 1-2 iters. Stacks on global best 1723.58.

brief-6 THE bet: rowscale -> FP16 + tau-override + R:=triu(Q^T A). CORRECTNESS PROVEN: validates ALL 3 guards incl invariance reseed-stress. tau-override makes householder_product orthonormal by construction (orth 2.6e-5, ~300x margin, even nearcollinear raw-tau 0.44->2.6e-5); R:=triu(Q^T A) makes factor residual=FP16 leakage (rowscale 1.69x). The bet's premise (checker needs only orth Q + R~Q^T A, not true V) HOLDS. BUT REGRESSES geomean 1723->1910 (mixed 4988->16591): the R-refine's Q^T A is batch-catastrophic in cuSOLVER (householder_product/orgqr 21915us; torch.ormqr/larfb 16591us) -- re-confirms brief-1's cuSOLVER-batch finding. tau-override-ALONE (path's R) fails the gate 1.45x -> R MUST be recomputed. A FAST R-refine needs a CUSTOM GEMM compact-WY Q^T A apply (not cuSOLVER). band/near-collinear stay exact-FP32 (factor 0.72x, fundamental). Honest regression committed.

Revert to parent (global best 1732, mixed 4984, all guards pass). brief-6 bet PROVEN CORRECT (cc77020 validates all guards: tau-override orth 2.6e-5, rowscale factor 1.69x) but cuSOLVER R-refine (orgqr 21915us / ormqr 16591us) regresses; tau-override-alone fails factor gate 1.45x so R must be recomputed; a fast R-refine needs a custom GEMM compact-WY Q^T A apply (not cuSOLVER) -- substantial C++ for a thin-margin win. Reverted pending manager's call on the custom-GEMM investment; brow infra preserved in cc77020.

Brief-6 RESOLVED: the checker-freedom bet (rowscale -> FP16 + tau-override + R:=triu(Q^T A)) is PROVEN CORRECT (commit cc77020 validates all 3 guards incl invariance reseed-stress: tau-override orth 2.6e-5 ~300x margin, rowscale factor 1.69x). Established that R MUST be recomputed (tau-override-alone fails the factor gate 1.45x) and that the cuSOLVER Q^T A is the bottleneck (householder_product/orgqr 21915us, torch.ormqr/larfb 16591us -- both batch-catastrophic on B200, re-confirming brief-1). Reverted HEAD to global best (2894322, ~1724, all guards pass); brow-split infra + qr_n512_brow_indices getter preserved in cc77020. Manager chose GO: next is brief-7 = build a fast custom GEMM-based compact-WY Q^T A apply (the keystone primitive unblocking the whole checker-freedom direction for W0 rowscale + W1 well-cond + W2 band).

GO on (A). Build a FAST REUSABLE custom GEMM-based compact-WY Q^T A apply (keystone primitive) -- cuSOLVER Q^T A is batch-catastrophic on B200 (16591-21915us) and blocks the ENTIRE checker-freedom direction (W0 rowscale, W1 well-cond probe, W2 band all need it). Apply the stored compact-WY V (FP16-factored reflectors) to A in OB=64 blocks via the EXISTING mmb + build_Minv batched-GEMM machinery (NOT cuSOLVER) to produce Q^T A so R:=triu(Q^T A) is cheap.
